_meanings: A follower of the Vaiśeṣika doctrine.

One
 of the six principal Darśanas or systems of Hindu philosophy founded by
 Kaṇāda; it differs from the Nyāya philosophy of Gautama in that it
 recognizes only seven instead of sixteen categories or heads of predicables
 (the earlier writers {%<ab>e. g.</ab>%} Kaṇāda recognizing only six), and lays
 particular stress upon Viśeṣa.
